n: Kitronik Autonomous Robotics Platform for Pico
t: A no-solder two-wheel robot buggy kit that a Raspberry Pi Pico drives.
steps: Buy the kit from Kitronik, The Pi Hut or another maker store. It costs about 41 British pounds.
Get a Raspberry Pi Pico with headers already soldered, a micro USB cable and four AA batteries.
Build the buggy with the printed booklet and push the Pico in with its USB plug facing the rear.
Install the free Thonny editor on your computer.
Copy the Kitronik PicoAutonomousRobotics.py file onto the Pico.
Run the motors tutorial example and watch the robot drive.
Try the line following and ultrasonic tutorials next.
meta: Open Code. From $51.95. A few stores.
